xaendarPlugin.summary: Creates the Vite plugin that compiles the templates and the stylesheets of the components ahead of time, and type-checks the project.
xaendarPlugin.description:
The plugin, named xaendar, goes in the plugins of the Vite configuration, after the transform of the standard decorators. The xd CLI adds it on its own, with the options read from xaendar.json. The options are described below; their type is XaendarPluginOptions.

For every component declared in a file ending with .xd.component.ts, the plugin reads the options of @WebComponent from the source code, validates and claims the selector, type-checks the template against the class, and adds to the module the imports of two virtual modules: the render function compiled from the template, and the CSSStyleSheet built from the stylesheet. A template or a stylesheet shared by several components is compiled once, into a module they all import. A @WebComponent in a TypeScript file with another name is an error.

Vite only strips the types, so the plugin checks them: a build type-checks the whole project once it ends, as tsc --noEmit does, and the dev server checks each TypeScript file as it serves it. The compiler options, strict ones included, come from the tsconfig.json of the directory Vite is started from, or of the nearest directory above it holding one: start Vite from the root of the project.

In the dev server, the plugin watches what each component depends on: its template, its stylesheet, the components its template imports, the classes it extends and the files its type check reads. Editing any of them compiles the component again.

members.customElements:
The patterns of the tag names of the custom elements of other libraries, such as Shoelace or an element written without Xaendar, which the templates use without importing them. In a pattern, * stands for any sequence of characters, and every other character stands for itself: sl-* matches sl-button and sl-icon-button, vanilla-stars only itself. A pattern must match the whole tag name.

Defaults to none: every tag with a hyphen used by a template must then be a component imported by it with @import, or the build fails. The CLI passes the customElements of xaendar.json.

The compiler treats a matching tag as a native element: its bindings write attributes, so the element receives strings, its attributes are not checked against any class, and $event has the type HTMLElementEventMap declares for the event, any for an event it does not declare. The library still has to define the element at run time. A tag that matches a pattern and is also a component imported by the template fails the build: keep the patterns specific to the other libraries. See Selectors and registration.
members.strictEvents: Whether the type check warns about the events the elements of a template do not declare: on a native element an event missing from HTMLElementEventMap (or the map of its namespace), on the tag of a component or in a directive an event that is neither one of its outputs nor a native event. Such an event may bubble up to the element from its content, so the binding is kept, with $event typed as Event, and the build and the editor only warn about its name. false turns the warning off; the elements of the customElements libraries never get it. Defaults to true. The CLI passes the strictEvents of xaendar.json, which the editor reads too.
members.ssr:
Renders the pages on the server. The modules evaluated by the environments of the server of Vite, such as ssr, register their templates compiled into HTML and their stylesheets as text, with @xaendar/ssr; the environment of the browser keeps the usual ones, and alone type-checks the project. entry is the module rendering a page, absolute or relative to the root of Vite: it exports render(url), returning the HTML, url being the path of the request with its query string, read with toSameOriginPath().

The dev server then renders every page it serves: it reads the index.html of the root of Vite, applies the plugins to it, and writes what render(url) returns in place of <!--xd-ssr-->. It loads the entry through the module graph of the server, so a changed component is rendered again at the next request, and a change to a module only the server loads reloads the page. The plugin sets the application type of Vite to custom, so that the dev server serves no index.html of its own. Defaults to none: every environment gets the templates of the browser. The CLI passes the ssr of xaendar.json. See Server-side rendering.

staticComponents makes a build find the static components, which it leaves out of the bundle of the browser. It pays off when the server renders each page and the browser never creates one, as in a multi-page application; a single-page application finds almost nothing, since its router creates the pages in the browser. Defaults to false.
members.staticReport: Whether the build tells what keeps each interactive component in the bundle of the browser, besides listing the static ones, what xd build --static-report asks for. Without ssr.staticComponents no component is searched, and the build says there is nothing to report. Defaults to false.

configuration.title: Adding it to the Vite configuration
configuration.body: A project driving Vite directly lists the plugin after the Babel transform of the standard decorators: the plugin adds its registration before the static block Babel generates in each decorated class. In the opposite order, every component fails with the error below.

cli.title: Projects run by the CLI
cli.body: xd start, xd build and xd test add Babel and the plugin to the configuration of vite.config.ts on their own, so the configuration does not list them. The CLI passes to the plugin the customElements, the strictEvents and the ssr of the xaendar.json found in the directory it is run from, none when the file or the fields are missing, the entry of ssr resolved against that directory.

errors.title: Reading the errors
errors.body: The messages of the plugin start with Xaendar:, and the ones of the type check with [TypeChecker], followed by the position in the template and the excerpt involved. A component that cannot be compiled fails the build; in the dev server it is left without its render function, and throws when it is connected. A TypeScript file with type errors is not served, and its errors show in the Vite overlay too. The Error encyclopedia lists the messages.

styles.title: Stylesheets
styles.body: A stylesheet can be a .css, .scss, .sass or .less file: any other extension fails to compile. Sass and Less files are compiled with the sass and less packages, optional peer dependencies that the project installs itself, and their imports are resolved at build time. Comments are then removed, and in vite build the CSS is also minified with Lightning CSS, unless build.cssMinify is false. Each file becomes one CSSStyleSheet, adopted by every component pointing to it. See Styling.

XaendarPluginOptions.summary: The type of the options of xaendarPlugin().
XaendarPluginOptions.description: The object passed to xaendarPlugin(), whose page describes each option. Every option is optional: xaendarPlugin() without arguments takes the defaults.

members.customElements: The patterns of the tag names of the custom elements of other libraries, such as sl-*, which the templates use like native elements. Defaults to none. See xaendarPlugin() for the syntax of the patterns and how the compiler treats the tags matching them.
members.strictEvents: Whether the type check warns about the events the elements of a template do not declare. Defaults to true. See xaendarPlugin().
members.ssr: The rendering on the server: entry is the module rendering a page, and staticComponents, false by default, whether a build finds the static components. Defaults to none. See xaendarPlugin().
members.staticReport: Whether the build tells what keeps each interactive component in the bundle of the browser, besides listing the static ones, what xd build --static-report asks for, when ssr.staticComponents makes it search them. Defaults to false.

buildLibrary.summary: Builds a library of components and directives into a package ready to be published, compiled ahead of time for the browser and, when the library renders on the server, for the server too.
buildLibrary.description:
It is what xd build runs in a workspace, for each library of the libs of xaendar.json. The library is compiled as the plugin compiles an application: its templates become render functions and its stylesheets CSSStyleSheets, type-checked with the tsconfig.json of its folder. An application imports its components with @import, without compiling them again.

The entry of the library and every module declaring a component or a directive become files of their own, so that an application loads only the components its templates use, and a @defer one of them alone. The code is an ES module, not minified, whose imports of @xaendar/* and of the dependencies and peer dependencies of the library stay imports, which the application resolves. The declarations are emitted by TypeScript, the paths of their imports written relative to each file, with the extension .js: the aliases of the paths of tsconfig.json do not reach the package.

The folder of the build is emptied first, then receives the code, the declarations, xaendar-manifest.json, the package.json of the package, built from the one of the library, and the README.md and the license of the library, when it has them. The build fails, before writing anything, on a component or a directive declared outside of the folder of the entry, on a selector declared twice, and on an input or an event whose type reads a name its module does not export, which the applications could not read.

members.name: The name of the package of the library, the one of its package.json (@acme/ui), which the manifest records. The files of the library can import it by this name, and the files beside its entry by @acme/ui/<path>: the build leads both to its sources.
members.root: The folder of the library, absolute or relative to the working directory. It holds the package.json of the library and the tsconfig.json its files are type-checked with, which, in a workspace, extends the one of the workspace.
members.entry: The module exporting what the library publishes, absolute or relative to its folder: src/public-api.ts by default. Its folder holds the sources: every component and directive of the library is declared under it, and the package keeps the paths of the modules relative to it.
members.outDir: The folder the package is written to, absolute or relative to the working directory, emptied first: npm publish publishes it as it is. xd build passes the outDir of the library in libs, dist/<folder of the library> by default.
members.ssr: Whether the library renders on the server. The build then compiles it a second time, for the server, into server/, which the exports of the package give to the condition xaendar-server, and the package requires @xaendar/ssr as an optional peer dependency. Without it, @hydrate, @client and the ssr option of @WebComponent are errors in its templates and components. Defaults to false.
members.customElements: The patterns of the tag names of the custom elements of other libraries its templates use like native elements, such as sl-*: see the option of the same name of xaendarPlugin(). Defaults to none.
members.strictEvents: Whether the type check of its templates warns about the events their elements do not declare: see the option of the same name of xaendarPlugin(). xd build passes the one of the library in libs, the one of the workspace when the library sets none. Defaults to true.
members.plugins: The plugins of Vite running before the Xaendar plugin, which the build adds on its own: the transform of the standard decorators with Babel, which the Xaendar plugin needs before it, as in the configuration of an application. xd build passes the Babel plugin it adds to the projects.
members.xaendarVersion: The version of Xaendar compiling the library, which the manifest records. The package requires @xaendar/core, and with ssr @xaendar/ssr, from this version up to the next major one (^), since the compiled code calls their runtime. xd build passes its own version.
members.dependencies: The libraries of the workspace the library depends on, by the name of their package, mapped to the folder of their build ({ '@acme/ui': '/ws/dist/ui' }): the library reads them from their declarations and their manifests, as an application installing them does, rather than compiling their sources again, and its code imports them by their name. Their builds must exist already: xd build builds the libraries of a workspace in this order. Defaults to none.

package.title: What the package holds
package.body: For a library @acme/ui whose entry exports a card, built into dist/ui, the folder holds the files below. The exports of its package.json list the entry and the module of each component and directive the entry exports, with their declarations, so that an application imports a component from the entry as well as by the path of its module (@acme/ui/card/card.xd.component). The modules of the components and of the directives, and the chunks, are listed in sideEffects, so that the bundler of an application never drops one it imports: importing the module of a component defines its element.
